newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila's foreign loan drawdowns hit $442 mln in Q1.
newsitem.headline: Manila's foreign loan drawdowns hit $442 mln in Q1.

text.p: The Philippines drew down $441.9 million in foreign loans in the first quarter of the year, up from $440.4 million a year earlier, the Coordinating Council of the Philippine Assistance Programme (CCPAP) said on Tuesday.
The CCPAP said the Asian Development Bank disbursed $102.7 million during the period, up from $47.1 million released in the same period last year.
World Bank released $56.6 million during the three-month period against last year's $111.1 million and Japan's Overseas Economic Cooperation Fund 27.9 billion yen versus 26.7 billion.
At present, there are $10.4 billion worth of foreign bilateral and multilateral loans financing 154 projects in the country. A total of $4.88 billion have been used so far.
